name: Doom of Mokhaiotl

mechanics.name: Standard Attacks
mechanics.description: Doom throws a single orb whose colour names the style: blue for magic, green for ranged, red for melee. The colour is only readable once the orb is already in the air.
mechanics.counterplay: Swap to the matching protection prayer as the orb launches. Red orbs only start appearing one delve down.

mechanics.name: Tongue Lash
mechanics.description: Doom whips its tongue at anyone standing in melee range, in place of the orb it would otherwise throw.
mechanics.counterplay: Keep Protect from Melee up any time you fight it from melee distance.

mechanics.name: Rock Throw
mechanics.description: Doom hurls a rock at your tile that shatters after a few ticks and rains styled projectiles across the marked ground. Deeper delves pack more projectiles into the same throw.
mechanics.counterplay: Step off the shadowed tile before the rock lands. Then pray against each projectile in the order it arrives.

mechanics.name: Melee Punish
mechanics.description: A yellow bar charges above Doom, ending in a beam that no prayer stops. While it charges it prays against everything except the style you are meant to answer it with.
mechanics.counterplay: Break the charge before the bar fills, with melee. Once it shields, only demonbane weapons get through.

mechanics.name: Demonic Larvae
mechanics.description: Grubs surface beside you and crawl for the centre of the arena. Any that reach Doom heal it and feed its charge; deeper delves colour them by prayer and eventually send giants.
mechanics.counterplay: Kill every grub before it arrives. A demonbane weapon drops one per hit, anything else takes two.

mechanics.name: Shockwave
mechanics.description: Doom slams the arena and rolls shockwaves outward across the whole floor. Deeper delves stack more waves onto the one slam.
mechanics.counterplay: Be behind an earthen shield before the slam lands. Nothing else in the arena blocks a wave.

mechanics.name: Volatile Earth
mechanics.description: Glowing earth erupts around the arena ahead of a shockwave. Striking two of them raises an earthen shield that walks toward the second.
mechanics.counterplay: Attack two nodes early and shelter behind the shield they raise. It clears acid off any tile it crosses.

mechanics.name: Acid Blood
mechanics.description: Doom sprays acidic blood onto the tiles around itself, and standing in it venoms you. The pools outlast the fight and only clear on the way down to the next delve.
mechanics.counterplay: Walk around the splatter. Earthen shields and the holy water from a melee punish both wipe it away.

mechanics.name: Demonic Shield
mechanics.description: Partway down its health Doom raises a demonic shield, charges its beam without pause and keeps feeding grubs into itself.
mechanics.counterplay: Break the shield with demonbane weapons and let exploding grubs chip it. Interrupt every charge until it drops.

mechanics.name: Burrow Charge
mechanics.description: Doom digs under the arena, marks a spot with a yellow eye and charges it, trampling anything on the way. Rocks drop from the ceiling while it is under.
mechanics.counterplay: Put a fallen rock between you and the charge, or stand clear of the line entirely.

mechanics.name: Double Rock Throw
mechanics.description: The deepest delves send two rock throws at once, so a second set of projectiles is already falling while you are still praying through the first.
mechanics.counterplay: Pray for the second explosion, not the first. Move once and let both sets land off your tile.

_ids: Every id here is named, not guessed: they come from Jagex's own gameval names (NpcID DOM_BOSS/DOM_BOSS_SHIELDED/DOM_BOSS_BURROWED/DOM_DEMONIC_ENERGY_*/DOM_SHOCKWAVE_PATH_NODE/DOM_SHOCKWAVE_SHIELD, AnimationID DOM_* and NPC_DEMONIC_GRUB_*, SpotanimID VFX_STANDARD_PROJECTILE_*/VFX_ROCK_PROJECTILE_*/VFX_BEAM_CHARGE_UP_01/VFX_DOOM_BOSS_BLOOD_SPLAT_*). The live cache's GAMEVALS index is not downloaded by the game client, and runelite-api 1.12.33 predates this boss entirely, so the names were read from RuneLite master's generated gameval sources and cross-checked against the ids present in the cache.
_previews: Doom is the first boss whose body animations are SKELETAL (sequence config opcode 13, zero classic frames), so FitZoom can only measure the static bind pose and the framemap compat check says nothing. The previews use model 56455 rather than the npc: 14707's models[0] is only the 1515-vertex centre body (X +/-142), while 56455 is the merged 1901-vertex whole boss (X +/-322) that Jagex's own Combat Achievements screen uses (struct 4933: model 56455, anim 12453 NPC_DOOM_BOSS_IDLE_CA, zoom 2500). Both carry the same 83-bone animaya rig, which is why the per-mechanic DOM_* animations play on it. The boss previews now ship at Jagex's own 2500 rather than the bind-pose fit of 1698: the first live pass showed the animated poses reaching well outside the bind pose and clipping the box, which is exactly the measurement the skeletal format denies us. shiftY tracks it (199 model units, projected at the shipped zoom). Larva recolor tables were checked against the model's face colours (D28): they repaint 0% of the faces, so their base model colours are already the ones you see in the fight. The sprite they ship as instead is about showing all three at once, not about colour.
_observed: Verified against a live delve on 2026-08-05, reaching at least delve 5 (the burrow fired). Ten of the eleven mechanics discovered; only double-rock-throw did not, which is expected at delve 8+. Four things the log settled that the cache could not. (1) The eight VFX_ROCK_PROJECTILE_PROJECTILE_ALT ids (3396-3403) NEVER fired, even though delve 4+ already throws three projectiles per rock. That is the evidence double-rock-throw needed: the ALT set is not the 2nd/3rd projectile of an ordinary throw, so claiming it will not unlock the mechanic early. It stays unproven in the other direction until someone reaches delve 8. (2) 3386/3387, the rock split, arrive as GRAPHIC and not as PROJECTILE -- they were curated as projectiles and would never have matched. Fixed, and worth remembering: a spotanim id says nothing about which event carries it. (3) The beam charge-up graphic 3412 never fired at all, so it is removed rather than left as a dead trigger; melee-punish unlocks off animation 12408 regardless. (4) The trigger log only prints animation, projectile and graphic, never npc-spawn -- but demonic-larvae, volatile-earth and demonic-shield were all discovered, which is what proves their npc-spawn ids matched. Deliberately NOT curated, all player-side and logged near the boss only because the player was standing there: projectiles 3367 (VFX_AYAK_NORMAL_PROJECTILE -- the Eye of Ayak is a Doom drop, so it will always appear in this fight), 1043, 1120, 1122, 2807, and graphics 2380, 2529, 2699. Animation 12422 DOM_DESPAWN is left unclaimed: it is the boss leaving, not a mechanic.
_note: Alternate preview animations to try if melee-punish reads poorly: 12409 DOM_BEAM_CHARGE_LOOP or 12411 DOM_BEAM_FIRE, and 12453 NPC_DOOM_BOSS_IDLE_CA as a neutral fallback for any mechanic. rock-throw's secondary is model 56498 (VFX_ROCK_PROJECTILE_LAUNCH_RANGE's own model, anim 12438), the whole boulder as it leaves Doom's hand -- not 56479, which is only the 43-vertex fragment that falls afterwards. Its zoom is deliberately NOT the FitZoom answer: the model's 482-unit bounding box is mostly empty air around a much smaller visible rock, so fitting the box (zoom 1872) rendered the boulder at about a third of the height it could have. 1150 fits the rock rather than the box, and lets the empty part of the envelope overhang. double-rock-throw is where its magic-coloured twin 56491 goes: the two launch models side by side read as the two simultaneous throws AND as the styles they arrive in, which is the closest the schema gets to showing both variants (all three at once alongside the boss would need a second secondary slot, dropped as issue #63). Neither uses the FitZoom answer either, for the same empty-envelope reason; both ride the 1150 that was eyeballed for rock-throw so the two boulders match scale. Neither shockwave nor burrow-charge is an animationChain, though both were curated as one first (issue #66, docs/DECISIONS.md D37) and the schema for it still ships. burrow-charge failed on looks: [12420 dive, 12421 underground idle] reads as an unexplained broken pose, because the preview box has no arena floor for the boss to be under (12417 DOM_BURROWED_MOVEMENT fails the same way for the same reason), so it is the dive alone, knowing it plays once and holds. shockwave failed on playback: [{12412,60},{12413,30},{12414,60}] plays its first segment, then pauses before the slam and after every slam, and never loops cleanly (issue #69, deferred past launch), so it is the slam alone. demonic-larvae is a bundled sprite (issue #64) rather than a model preview, for two reasons: the mechanic's whole point is that colour names the prayer and only a sprite can show all three at once, and the grub models carry no rig at all (no framemap groups, no animaya bones), so NPC_DEMONIC_GRUB_WALK could only cycle their alpha and read as jitter rather than crawling. That is also why the multi-secondary generalisation (issue #63) was dropped. See issue #61.
